text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Right-wing Popular Party (PP) will rethink its position on the government's 1997 budget proposals, PP leader Manuel Monteiro told the paper.
- Financially strapped companies which implement the so-called Mateus Plan could generate 500 billion escudos for the Portuguese economy by 1999, according to Economy Minister Augusto Mateus.
- Security will be discussed in parliament today. The government will try to show that the crackdown on crime is one of its priorities.
- The government to offer no more than 2.5 percent pay rise in 1997 civil service pay round starting today.
- In today's parliamentary debate, the government will announce its calendar to put a further 7,000 police onto the streets in the next three years.
- Prime Minister Antonio Guterres offers 2.5 percent salary rises for civil servants but trade unions want a rise of between 4.5 and 7 percent.
